questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to learn French and the French approach to philosophy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:

questions.answer: Not that easy, but I think you just have to be patient and wait until they contact you. Things are generally a bit more "loose" than at UCPH when it comes to registering for classes, exams, etc.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The local exchange coordinator sends a link to an excel-file where you have to register the courses you want and a document with descriptions of all the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator provided all the help that was needed

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was accepted to all the classes I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just wait until they contact you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is generally a higher level than in UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, since all of my classes were 100 % lectures by the teacher, i.e. no group work or anything like that. There were not even any assignments or homework during the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Metaphysique phenomenologique, Hegel et l'être, Systematicité et historicité, Dynamique et metaphysique

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are so many courses and they change each semester, so its not really possible to answer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is very nice to go to the Bois de Vincennes in the weekend if you want a bit of nature and fresh air

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local students are not very welcoming so they are not going to  unless maybe if you very actively try to befriend them. There are no parties or friday bars at the university either, so it is not very easy to establish a relationship with the local students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Parisians are a bit rude and arrogant, but don't take it personally.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, museums

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have a good level of French before the semester starts. Try to learn the specific French genres of papers, like dissertation and explicate de texte. Also be aware that you might have to write the exams in handwriting and not on the computer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offers a personal tutor for exchange students, i.e. a local student that can help you with questions. I would highly recommend accepting that offer, because they can help you with many things regarding the exams, the French types of assignments etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The classes/teaching

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Completing the exams in French

questions.answer: Yes
